description: GCAM is the Global Change Analysis Model maintained by the Joint Global Change Research Institute at Pacific Northwest National Laboratory. It represents interacting energy, water, land and economic systems linked through markets, trade and environmental effects. Users supply population, productivity, technology and policy assumptions to generate scenarios of resource use, energy supply and demand, land allocation and emissions. The current README describes a global run period from 1990 to 2100 with annual results computed at one- to five-year intervals; regional detail varies by component. Source code, inputs and documentation are public and free under the Educational Community License 2.0. The repository contains the R data system and C++ model code. GCAM can support long-term infrastructure-transition and resource-demand studies. A limitation is that results are conditional on scenario assumptions and version-specific representations, not forecasts of actual investment. Existing model-gcam-china is a regional derivative, not the general repository. No model runs or input downloads were performed.
